To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the humanized antibody CAMPATH‐ 1H can be expressed by myeloma cells and is functionally similar to the antibody expressed by CHO cells.

(1) CAMPATH‐1M, a humanized antibody, was successfully expressed in transfected myelomacells; (2) the nucleotide sequence of CAMPATH‐M heavy and light chain genes is shown; (3) the effector functions, ADCC and CDC, of myeloma‐ and CHO‐derived CAMPATH-1M are similar.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of humanized MoAbs and the use of myeloma cells for the expression of these antibodies in a humanized form.
the development of CAMPATH‐H, an immunotoxin based on a chimeric antibody directed to the surface of human lymphocytes.
the development of CAMPATH‐H, a human‐like antibody with potential therapeutic applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
myeloma cells can be engineered to generate high levels of humanized MoAb and the effector mechanisms of the antibody are identical in both CHO and myeloma cell‐derived material.
CAMPATH‐1 is an effective MoAb with a wide range of effector mechanisms, that can be expressed in a variety of cell types, including myeloma cells, and can be expressed in high yield.
CAMPATH‐1M is a superior product to CAMPATH‐1G, in terms of both antibody dependent cellular cytolytic and complement dependent cytolytic activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the myeloma cell system is a useful tool for generating CAMPATH‐1 antibodies, but CHO cells are the preferred system for the large scale production of the antibody.
CAMPATH‐1G, CAMPATH‐1M and CAMPATH‐1N have been humanized to CAMPATH‐1A, CAMPATH‐H and CAMPATH‐IgG1, respectively.
the CAMPATH‐ 1H MoAb can be produced in myeloma cells at a level similar to CHO cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is feasible to generate high‐level expression of humanized MoAb from transfected myelomacells.

CAMPATH‐1 is an excellent antibody to study the mechanisms of antibody dependent cellular cytotoxicty and complement dependent cytotoxictly, but the expression levels of the antibody from CHO cells are much higher than from myeloma cells.
it is possible to achieve high level expression of CAMPATH‐I H in myeloma cells and this approach may be of use for production of other MoAbs.
